about: The evangelium of the formulary “21st Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus told His disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven has been likened to a king who wished to call his servants to account. And when he had begun the reckoning, one was presented to him who owed him ten thousand talents. But since he had nothing with which to repay, his lord ordered that he be sold, and his wife and his children and everything he had, and that repayment be made. But that servant fell down and implored him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything. And the lord of that servant, moved with pity, released him and forgave him the debt. But when that servant had gone out, he found a fellow servant of his who owed him a hundred denarii; and seizing him, he was choking him, saying: Pay back what you owe. And his fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything. But he would not; instead he went off and put him in prison until he paid back the debt. Now when his fellow servants saw what was happening, they were deeply grieved, and they came and told their lord all that had taken place. Then his lord called him and said to him: Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. Ought not you also, then, to have had pity on your fellow servant, even as I had pity on you? And his lord, being angry, delivered him to the torturers until he repaid the whole debt. So also will My heavenly Father do to you, if you do not forgive, each one his brother, from your hearts.

a.g: his master ordered him to be sold
